approved: Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (Customs) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package of three charges bills that support the Recycling and Waste Reduction Bill 2020.
The package would let the Commonwealth recover the costs of regulating waste material exports by setting charges in future regulations.
The charges themselves, including amounts and who pays, would be set later by the Governor-General in regulations.
The bill would create a framework for imposing charges on waste material exports.
It would allow the government to recover costs of regulating those exports.
The bill would not set the charge amounts or impose any financial impacts itself.
Exporters of regulated waste materials and the Commonwealth government.

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2020-10-26.193.6) that the debate be not adjourned. In other words, they voted to continue the debate.
The Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (Customs) Bill 2020 imposes customs duties as part of the waste export ban charging package, with charge amounts and liable parties to be set by regulation.

The member for Blue Mountains supported the Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (Customs) Bill 2020, citing that only 12% of plastic is recycled in Australia and noting that local students had campaigned against plastic bags, while criticising the government for seven years of inaction on waste and climate change. The member moved that the debate be adjourned.

The speaker moved to rescind the third readings of five recycling and waste reduction bills and to immediately call them on again, with a Minister moving each third reading and the question put without debate.
